web_evidence.title: Excerpt from The Immortalists by Chloe Benjamin
web_evidence.note: A sustained, publisher-permitted excerpt from chapter 1 narrates Simon and the other Gold siblings externally while entering Simon's perceptions; it contains no participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Now & at the Hour of Our Death: Q&A with 'The Immortalist' Author Chloe Benjamin
web_evidence.note: Benjamin explains that the novel stays with one sibling at a time across four post-prologue parts and explicitly identifies the technique as close third, establishing that changing focal characters do not change grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Chloe Benjamin Writing Styles in The Immortalists
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly describes a third-person narrator, predominantly focalized through one Gold sibling in each part, with occasional omniscient access to others.

web_evidence.title: The Immortalists Study Guide
web_evidence.note: The guide's key facts identify the point of view as third-person limited, with each section focalized through one of the four protagonists.

search_log: Searched "The Immortalists Chloe Benjamin excerpt publisher first chapter" and opened the sustained BookBrowse excerpt, which states that it is reproduced by permission of G. P. Putnam's Sons.
Searched "The Immortalists Chloe Benjamin point of view third person narrator" and opened explicit whole-book descriptions from BookRags and LitCharts.
Searched "The Immortalists Chloe Benjamin review four sections third-person" and opened the ZYZZYVA author interview, where Benjamin discusses the four-part structure and close-third technique.

Searched Penguin Random House materials and opened the publisher-hosted author Q&A PDF; it discussed premise and characters but did not explicitly identify narrative person, so it was not used as person evidence.

Reviewed general newspaper and review results describing the four sibling sections; these were useful for discovery but were not treated as person evidence when they did not explicitly discuss narration.
person_note: The novel's base narration is close third person, shifting focalization among Simon, Klara, Daniel, and Varya in separate sections without changing grammatical person. Numerous Goodreads passages independently show external narration with sustained access to those characters' private thoughts, and the authorized excerpt agrees. Benjamin's author Q&A and two explicit whole-book guides confirm that the multiple viewpoints remain third person. The apparent first-person event quotes q03244 and q03263 are clipped character discourse, consistent with the many dialogue quotations, not autonomous first-person sections. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration was found.
